what: The lane's brief said `cargo test -p` for each crate touched, and cargo cannot build blaze-std: `cargo +nightly-2026-10-27 check -p blaze-std --tests` ends in 10 errors (contracts' `-> (r: T)`, `where const`, `core::reflect`, three unknown blaze features). The lane was told to run no blaze, so bstd's new code (simtest.rs, the Io::submit hook, tests/simtest.rs) could not be built by anything allowed.
cost: about an hour of design to put the runner where cargo reaches it (blaze-core), and a scratch port to run the bstd side at all
cause: rule blaze-uses-its-extensions meets rule blaze-builds-blaze's cargo dev loop, as in A10; a brief for bstd work written as if cargo checked bstd
whys: bstd's tests ran nowhere in this lane
only a blaze compiles bstd and lanes run no blaze
the dev loop's builder (cargo) and the language bstd is written in differ
nothing in the loop compiles bstd per lane report
class: code only a blaze can check, written in a loop whose checker is cargo: it is unverified until someone else runs a blaze
prevention: the main agent's per-crate check within minutes of a lane's report has to be `blaze check -p blaze-std --tests` on blaze-vm for any lane that touches bstd; state: not built here
workaround: a scratch copy of crates/blaze-std outside the tree, with path dependencies into the worktree, that rustc compiles after these cuts: the four contracts (`-> (r: T) ensures ..` to `-> T`), every `where const {..}`, `core::reflect::MemoPoint` and `code_id_of` in eval.rs, the bodies of own/raw.rs's const fns, own.rs's two BTreeMap/BTreeSet `Owns` impls, `Shares::join`, and the three blaze features; tests own, eval and cell left out. There `cargo test --lib` ran 141 passed, 3 failed against 132 passed, 3 failed on the base commit (the same three). It proves nothing about blaze's build of bstd.
